_comment: Maximum finding counts per tool. A ratchet: scripts/lint_ratchet.py fails when a
run finds MORE than max_findings, and fails when a commit RAISES max_findings
(against the merge base with main) without a `Ratchet-Exempt: <why>` trailer.
When a run finds fewer, lower the number in the same change to lock the gain in.
Measured 2026-09-19 at commit a61112a, unchanged at 06fd061 (after the ruff safe autofixes and
the 6768cc6 MCP logging fix, which removed mypy's 20 call-arg errors):
ruff  451 findings over 103 files -- ANN001 110, E501 98, ANN202 89, W293 43,
ANN201 22, E402 19, ... (backend/: tests 260, src 163, scripts 28)
mypy  46 errors in 18 files, 59 source files checked -- import-untyped 10,
no-any-return 6, index 6, type-arg 5, unused-ignore 4, var-annotated 4, ...
No eslint entry, on purpose. frontend/ has no eslint.config.* and eslint 9
refuses to run without one (exit 2 before inspecting a single file), so the CI
lint step has never inspected anything. .gnomon/ci.sh reports it SKIPPED with
that reason rather than inventing a rule set to measure. Whoever adds the config
adds an `eslint` entry here in the same change (tool = eslint, cwd = frontend,
args = ["src/"]); until then lint_ratchet.py refuses to run an undeclared entry.
Lowered 2026-09-19 by the backend rewire onto causal-core (heuristic skills removed):
The args are the SAME ones the tool runs with here and in .gnomon/ci.sh, so the
number and the command that produced it cannot drift apart.
2026-09-21: 442 -> 441 after the verdict-binding change. The new code is clean; the net gain is two import-order findings fixed in files it touched.

2026-09-21: ruff 441 -> 424 after the .env loader moved out of src/api/main.py's import block into src/env_bootstrap.py (19 E402 findings describing one deliberate ordering constraint, now stated as an import). mypy 40 -> 39: pandas joined the stubless-module list beside firebase_admin and neo4j.

2026-09-24: ruff 424 -> 417. Ten F841 unused locals and two B007 unused loop variables removed; three of them were the tell for something real -- a discarded `user_ref` where the submitter's identity should have been recorded, a discarded `original_action` in a guardian test that therefore never compared the row it was named for, and a `for` loop in planning.py whose only statement was `continue`. mypy unchanged at 39.

2026-09-25: the three kernel packages join at zero (mypy --strict via each pyproject's [tool.mypy]). They were clean and nothing kept them so; causal-core 26 files, causal-decision 10, causal-mcp 4. Run with the kernel environment's mypy, not the backend's.

2026-09-25: eslint joins at zero. frontend/eslint.config.mjs (Next's core-web-vitals + typescript) was added and the 20 findings it surfaced were fixed, so frontend-eslint runs instead of being SKIPPED as it had been since it was declared.

2026-09-25: bandit joins at zero MEDIUM+ (LOW is reported, not counted). bandit-backend runs with backend/pyproject.toml's [tool.bandit], which skips B101 (assert) and B608 (SQL built from strings) for the whole tree -- a config decision this entry inherits, not one it made: with B608 enabled, backend/src has 13 MEDIUM findings (f-strings inside text() in src/api/governance.py, incidents.py, interventions.py and src/semantic_layer/registry.py). They were not reviewed one by one in this change, and the blanket skip stays until they are. bandit-packages runs bandit's defaults over packages/*/src. The three B310 urlopen findings (src/connectors/prometheus.py, causal_core/bench/ihdp.py and lalonde.py) were fixed in code, not annotated.

2026-09-25 (septa-50): the B608 and B101 skips are gone; backend/pyproject.toml's [tool.bandit] skips no rule. The 13 B608 sites were reviewed one by one and none carried a request value into SQL text: governance.py's audit-log WHERE, and registry.py's list_entities, list_fragments and list_pending_assumptions, joined fixed condition strings whose values were bound; incidents.py built a numbered placeholder list and a fixed status clause; interventions.py a fixed incident clause; registry.py's promote_to_approved, reject_draft and list_pending_review_queue interpolated a table and column name from a closed object_type mapping. Each is now a literal statement, an expanding bind parameter, or SQLAlchemy Core over a lightweight untyped table with every value a named bindparam() given at execution, as text() binds were (a literal compared to a column takes a type from the value and asyncpg renders a ::VARCHAR cast PostgreSQL refuses against UUID and JSONB columns) -- no # nosec. backend/tests/integration/test_sql_filters_bound.py pins the queries' results on seeded rows and sends SQL-shaped values through them. B101 is LOW, so it is reported, not counted; src's one assert (api/decisions.py, a type-narrowing after a validator) became an explicit check. bandit-backend stays at 0 MEDIUM+.

ruff-scripts._why: The gate scripts themselves. Zero, and it stays zero: a gate whose own code does not lint is not one to trust. Ruff's default rule set (no project config at the repo root).

mypy-causal-core._why: packages/causal-core/src under its own strict config. Zero, and it stays zero.

mypy-causal-decision._why: packages/causal-decision/src under its own strict config. Zero, and it stays zero.

mypy-causal-mcp._why: packages/causal-mcp/src under its own strict config. Zero, and it stays zero.

eslint._why: frontend/src under Next.js core-web-vitals + typescript. Zero, and it stays zero.

bandit-backend._why: backend/src and backend/mcp_server under backend/pyproject.toml's [tool.bandit]. MEDIUM and HIGH count; zero, and it stays zero.

bandit-packages._why: Every packages/*/src (the glob is expanded against the tree, so a new package is scanned the day it lands), bandit's default rule set. MEDIUM and HIGH count; zero, and it stays zero.
